round: 2026-10-02 review (the mega review of the preview site)
note: October 2, 2026: the owner went through every toy on the preview site and named the sounds to change; every toy he called perfect or fine stays as it is. Two notes cover every toy: when a tap pauses an effect, its sound must pause and resume with it; and a toy's first tap often sounds late (later taps are in sync). He still wants subtle, realistic sounds, often real recordings, with no wind unless it belongs, no motor 'vroom', no buzz or horn and no robotic tones. The full review is docs/reviews/2026-10-02-mega-review/review.md.

raspberry.said: The raspberry sounds a little bit too much like bubbles.
raspberry.note: It sounds too much like bubbles.
raspberry.plan: A real juicy squish as the drupelets break off, then a soft tap for each one landing on the table, and a small squish as they come back (no bubbles).

blackberry.said: The raspberry sounds a little bit too much like bubbles. The blackberry does as well.
blackberry.note: Like the raspberry, it sounds too much like bubbles.
blackberry.plan: A darker, deeper real squish, the drupelets tapping down on the table as they bounce, and a soft squish as they spring back (no bubbles).

star-cookie.said: The cinnamon star cookie sounds almost like a zipper unzipping. It doesn't actually sound like a cookie breaking apart or anything like that.
star-cookie.note: It sounds like a zipper, not a cookie breaking apart.
star-cookie.plan: A real crisp snap and crumble as it breaks, and a small soft crumble as it puts itself back together.

mandeltorus.said: The mandalorian is a little too robotic sounding. … And quite frankly, we could make the Mandel torus have something kind of similar in terms of the sound effect.
mandeltorus.note: It sounds too robotic; he'd like something similar to the Mandelbulb's sound, which he loves.
mandeltorus.plan: Like the Mandelbulb: a low drone with a ratchet as the rings start to turn, and again as they lock back.

garden-gnome.said: The garden gnome is a little weird. I'm not sure about this one. I don't really like the chirp sound that it makes at the beginning.
garden-gnome.note: A little weird; he doesn't like the chirp at the start.
garden-gnome.plan: A soft stone thud as the gnome lands from its hop, and a match-like flare and soft flame as its lantern lights (no chirp, no click).

lantern.said: I don't like the click sound that the lantern makes. So if we could find something else that's more suitable.
lantern.note: He doesn't like the click; he wants something more suitable.
lantern.plan: A real match strike and a soft flame catching when it lights; a real puff blowing it out.

wooden-elephant.said: The wooden elephant should actually have an elephant-like trumpet sound, like the real sound of an elephant making its trumpet sound. Elephants have a characteristic sound that comes out of their snout or their nose, so we should use that.
wooden-elephant.note: It should trumpet like a real elephant.
wooden-elephant.plan: A light wooden knock, then a real elephant trumpeting as the trunk lifts.

alarm-clock.said: The alarm clock within the photo real category could sound a little bit more like a real alarm clock. This currently sounds almost like a wooden instrument. I don't know how to describe it, but it doesn't sound very much like an alarm clock. … The alarm clock here in the Open Me category, kind of like the other alarm clock in the Photo Real category, if I'm not mistaken, should sound more realistic.
alarm-clock.note: It sounds like a wooden instrument, not an alarm clock; it should sound like a real one.
alarm-clock.plan: A real mechanical twin-bell alarm ringing while the clock rattles (2.3 s).

vintage-camera.said: The vintage camera, the flash should sound more realistic. Right now it sounds kind of like too clicky.
vintage-camera.note: The flash is too clicky; it should sound realistic.
vintage-camera.plan: A real vintage press camera: a soft shutter and the whoomph of the flash powder.

carrot-cake.said: The carrot cake sound is pretty underwhelming. I guess it's acceptable, but it's really simple. I guess we can leave it. I don't know. If you can find something more suitable, that would be fine.
carrot-cake.note: Acceptable but underwhelming and very simple; a better one would be welcome, otherwise leave it.
carrot-cake.plan: A softer knife slide, a moist crumb as the slice lifts out, and the same soft plate thud.

cat-statue.said: The cat statue should actually have a cat meowing instead of whatever that noise is that it makes.
cat-statue.note: It should meow like a real cat.
cat-statue.plan: A soft stone scrape as the head turns, then a real cat's meow as it tilts.

horse-statue.said: The horse statue should actually have a horse like whinny or neigh. There's a certain sound that a horse makes. I think you maybe tried to replicate that here, but it actually sounds kind of like some sort of whistle, which is not quite right.
horse-statue.note: The whinny sounds like a whistle; it should be a real horse whinny or neigh.
horse-statue.plan: A soft stone scrape, a real horse's whinny as it rears, and a stone thud as it lands.

tin-can-real.said: (October 2, 2026, review) It sounds like somebody plays a little drum and then a coin, like a metal quarter, is rolling around on the ground. ... It could just sound kind of metallic as it rolls, but I don't need the drum either.
tin-can-real.note: Drop the drum hit and the coin-like ring; just a plain metallic roll.
tin-can-real.plan: Now: One real recording of an empty can rolling on a hard floor, slowing and settling; no drum hit, no coin ring (Sound C).

donut.said: (October 2, 2026, review) It kind of sounds almost too wet.
donut.note: Sounds too wet; find a better one (right direction).
donut.plan: Now: A soft, dry tear as it pulls apart (a real bread tear) and a soft pat as the halves meet; nothing wet (Sound C).

knot.said: (October 6, 2026, walkthrough) The neon knot sounds like somebody taking a shit. ... Seriously, please pick something else. You can use the same sound as we use for the other knots. I do not care. But not this. This sounds dirty.
knot.note: The jelly sounds dirty; pick something else (the other knots' sound is fine).
knot.plan: Now: the torus knot's sound, timed to this knot: it strains as the loops tie tighter, then lets go with a soft thump and swish as it relaxes; no jelly (Sound D).

planet.said: The tiny planet, it's too much wind. It's kind of loud and almost hurts the ears. There are other toys that have a similar wind effect. For some of them, the wind sound is fine. I may mention those and tell you that that's fine, but generally the wind sound is just a little too overwhelming for a lot of the toys that use it, and the tiny planet is an example of that.
planet.note: Too much wind: loud enough to hurt the ears (the wind is too strong on many toys).
planet.plan: A quiet, darker breeze and a soft low whoosh as the clouds race round.

tennis-ball.said: The tennis ball does not sound like a tennis ball. It sounds more like a ping pong ball right now. If we can make it sound a little bit more like a real tennis ball, I'd appreciate that. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
tennis-ball.note: It sounds like a ping-pong ball; it should sound like a real tennis ball.
tennis-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown tennis ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

baseball.said: The baseball, the sound is nearly perfect, but when it gets hit by the invisible bat or whatever, it doesn't sound like it's being hit by, like, a bat. We can make it sound like it's being hit by a wooden bat. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
baseball.note: Nearly perfect, but the hit should sound like a wooden bat.
baseball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown baseball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

softball.said: The softball is kind of the same situation as the baseball. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
softball.note: Like the baseball: the hit should sound like a real bat.
softball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown softball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

beach-ball.said: The beach ball sounds a little too cartoony when it bounces.
beach-ball.plan: A real plastic beach-ball bounce each time it lands (no boing), and a light slap as it's punched up.

golf-ball.said: The golf ball is okay. I think that it's okay. Yeah, never mind. The golf ball is fine, I think. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
golf-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown golf ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

bowling-ball.said: For the bowling ball, I feel like we can make it sound just a little bit more like a bowling ball rolling on the bowling alley floor, and then when it hits the invisible pins, those need to sound like actual pins falling down. There is a real sound. You could probably find a sound pack that contains that that's realistic. Right now it just sounds a little too much like a toy. Real pins, like bowling alley pins, have a characteristic sound that you can find that's pretty consistent. This is close, but it's not quite right. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
bowling-ball.note: Close, but too toy-like: it should sound like a ball rolling down a real lane and real pins falling.
bowling-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown bowling ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

pool-ball.said: The pool ball sounds a little too high-pitched. It almost sounds like the pool ball is hollow or something. It should have the sound that's made when somebody actually hits, like, a pool ball with a pool stick. So it should sound a bit more solid, if that makes any sense. You can also probably find that. It's a pretty characteristic sound. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
pool-ball.note: Too high-pitched and hollow; it should sound solid, like a real cue striking a pool ball.
pool-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown pool ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

pickleball.said: I've never played pickleball, so I don't know if the whistling sound is realistic. It's kind of annoying. If we could change that, I'd appreciate it, unless it's really realistic. Maybe we could change how the whistle sounds at the very least. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
pickleball.note: The whistling is annoying; change it unless it's truly realistic.
pickleball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown pickleball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

marble.said: (October 2, 2026, review) The marble is a little too loud. The sound is close. ... It's just, like, kind of annoyingly loud by default. (Hands-on H1, October 8, 2026) New: its landing in Hands-on, to hear on the Sound Board. Its tap sound is unchanged.
marble.note: Same sound, quieter by default (or a slightly better real marble recording).
marble.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown marble lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft. The tap keeps the same real marble roll, about 6 dB quieter (Sound C).

solar-system.said: The solar system is pretty cool. I don't know if we could make it sound a little bit less robotic or electronic. I don't know if that makes any sense to you. If we have to keep it the way it is, it's fine.
solar-system.note: Pretty cool, but a little less robotic or electronic would be better; it's fine to keep if needed.
solar-system.plan: No synth chord: a soft whoosh as the planets swing into line, a warm flare as the corona shows, and a whoosh as they swing on.

mercury.said: Mercury is kind of weird. I don't know if it matches what is supposed to be happening here. So this has to do with heat, right? So I'm looking at the description of Mercury, and it spins fast while the side facing the sun glows red hot and shimmers. This doesn't really sound like that, if that makes any sense.
mercury.note: It doesn't match the effect (a fast spin while the sunlit side glows red hot and shimmers).
mercury.plan: A quick spin whoosh, then a low roar of heat and a soft searing sizzle while the day side glows, fading as it cools (no tone).

venus.said: Venus uses that wind sound, but I think it's fine in this case.

earth.said: I think that for the Earth, it doesn't need to have such a dramatic wind sound.
earth.plan: The same ocean wash (a little softer) and chime, with the wind turned right down (softer, shorter and quieter).

mars.said: Mars kind of has, like, a weird wind sound to it, but I think it's okay. Maybe we could improve it a little bit.
mars.note: The wind is a little weird; okay, but could be a bit better.
mars.plan: The dust storm is quieter and darker: a softer hiss of dust and a lower wind.

saturn.said: I don't really like the robotic kind of, like, noise that plays with Saturn.
saturn.note: He doesn't like the robotic noise.
saturn.plan: Two soft icy sweeps as the waves ripple out across the rings, with a faint glitter (no synth shimmer).

uranus.said: For Uranus, I don't really like the little bell or whatever that noise is that plays at the beginning. And it doesn't seem to make any noises as it rolls. We don't need to have, like, a really loud wind noise as it kind of rolls, but it would be nice if there was, like, some little effect there.
uranus.note: Drop the bell-like tone at the start; add a small sound while it rolls (not loud wind).
uranus.plan: A soft low rumble as it rolls to the right, and again as it rolls back (no bell).

neptune.said: Neptune uses that wind sound. I think it's okay here.

aurora-planet.said: (October 2, 2026, review) we can make the wind sound a little bit less dramatic
aurora-planet.plan: Now: The same aurora air, much lower and gentler (Sound C).

asteroid.said: The asteroid doesn't really sound like it's breaking apart.
asteroid.note: It doesn't sound like it's breaking apart.
asteroid.plan: A rock crack and a muffled boom, real rocks crumbling apart, a soft grinding as the rubble comes back, and the stone settling.

comet.said: The comet sounds more like wind or like a waterfall. I'd like to change that and make it sound more like something that's on fire, unless that's unrealistic.
comet.note: It sounds like wind or a waterfall; it should sound more like something on fire.
comet.plan: A real burning torch roaring as the jets and tails flare, fading as they die back.

meteor.said: (October 2, 2026, review) The meteor still doesn't really sound like it explodes at the end. ... you can use that same sound for the meteor, because the star sound is basically perfect.
meteor.note: It should audibly explode at the end: reuse the star's burst sound, in sync.
meteor.plan: Now: The streak's fire, then the star's own burst (over a short crack) as it explodes at 0.37 s, in time with the fireball (Sound C).

star.said: The star uses a robotic sort of song type of thing. I'd almost prefer that that's not there, and then we have some sounds that, like, kind of have it bursting like an explosion. I want it to be more realistic sound effects, but I don't want it to be, like, overwhelming wind or other stuff like that, if that makes any sense.
star.note: Drop the robotic song; realistic sounds of it bursting like an explosion, without overwhelming wind.
star.plan: A deep stellar roar as it swells, low throbs as the red giant pulses, a real explosion as it puffs off its shell, and a soft roar as a new star lights.

pulsar.said: The pulsar uses that, like, acceleration sound, the vroom kind of sound that's like a buzz. It's really annoying. I want to use something else, and I don't like the clicking that it makes. We should do something different, make it sound more epic.
pulsar.note: The "vroom" buzz and the clicking are annoying; it should sound more epic.
pulsar.plan: A deep boom and rumble as it spins up, and a deep pulse with each flash instead of a tick.

black-hole.said: For the black hole, we could make it a little more dramatic, that low buzzing noise as the star spirals into it. It's just a little too robotic sounding.
black-hole.note: The low buzz as the star spirals in should be more dramatic and less robotic.
black-hole.plan: A deep growing roar as the star spirals in, a rushing whoosh, a huge low boom as it plunges, and the gas swirling down after it.

star-cluster.said: (October 2, 2026, review) it sounds like kind of like a wind sound or something. It could be a little bit less overwhelming
star-cluster.plan: Now: Two faint, soft swells of air; much quieter, no hiss (Sound C).

planetary-nebula.said: Yeah, the Ring Nebula, it has, like, that weird robotic music. We should change it completely.
planetary-nebula.note: The robotic music is weird; change it completely.
planetary-nebula.plan: A small burst as the star flares, a whoosh as the shock ring expands, and a deep soft boom as it pushes the main ring out.

nebula.said: The nebula, kind of similar to the star cluster, like the little chimes or whatever you want to call that, little bells. I don't quite like it. I know that we have stars here, so we can maybe just change it a little bit.
nebula.note: Like the star cluster, he doesn't like the little chimes; change it a little.
nebula.plan: A soft fiery flare for each of the seven new stars as it lights (no chimes).

supernova.said: The supernova, it doesn't really sound like an explosion. It sounds more like the ocean or, like, wind. So we should change that.
supernova.note: It sounds like the ocean or wind, not an explosion.
supernova.plan: A real deep explosion with a long rumble, over the fiery roar.

spiral-galaxy.said: The spiral galaxy is probably fine. It just sounds... Yeah, I think that that one's okay.

virus.said: For the virus, we don't need that little sound that plays at the end of the animation.
virus.note: Drop the little sound at the end of the animation.
virus.plan: The same ripple, squish and pops as the copies bud, without the shimmer at the end.

red-blood-cell.said: For the red blood cell, I feel like we could make the sound different. It sounds almost like a little whistle of some sort. I don't know how to describe the sound, but it's a little weird.
red-blood-cell.note: It sounds like a little whistle; a little weird.
red-blood-cell.plan: A soft, gel-like squish as it stretches into a crescent, and a soft wobble as it relaxes (no squeaks).

neuron.said: The neuron could sound more like electricity, if that makes any sense. Right now it just sounds like clicking. It's just like a lot of clicking.
neuron.note: It's just a lot of clicking; it should sound more like electricity.
neuron.plan: A real crackling electric arc running down the axon, and a brighter burst at the terminals.

astrocyte.said: The astrocyte is almost perfect, but the first sound that's made, that, like, noise that's played when you click on the astrocyte at the beginning, can we change that and make it sound less robotic or just a different tune?
astrocyte.note: Almost perfect; only the first sound should be less robotic or a different tune.
astrocyte.plan: A soft airy swell as the calcium wave spreads (no synth shimmer), then the same soft wash as the vessel widens.

dna.said: (October 2, 2026, review) the zipper sound doesn't seem exactly synchronized. Maybe we could find a different zipper sound
dna.note: The zip isn't quite in sync with the unzipping; sync it or find a better zipper recording (flexible).
dna.plan: Now: The real zipper timed to the strands: a quick zip as they fly open, a slower one as they close up (3.45 s) (Sound C).

white-blood-cell.said: The white blood cell uses maybe a little bit more clicking than I'd prefer, but it's mostly good.
white-blood-cell.note: Mostly good, with a bit less clicking.
white-blood-cell.plan: A soft squishy membrane reaching out (no flutter clicks), the same gulp as it swallows, and a quieter fizz as it digests.

chromosome.said: For the chromosome, I'd almost prefer that it's just, like, more realistic sound effects and not the, like, guitar string or instrument string.
chromosome.note: Realistic sound effects, not a plucked string.
chromosome.plan: A soft sticky tear as the chromatids pull apart, and a soft squish as they come back together (no string, no clacks).

mitochondrion.said: (October 2, 2026, review) I really don't like that vroom or, like, buzz or motor sound. ... It could be, like, the sound of maybe, like, a furnace
mitochondrion.note: No motor, vroom or buzz. A 'powerhouse' sound such as a furnace; try a few and pick.
mitochondrion.plan: Now: A real gas furnace lighting with a soft whoomp and a warm roar as it powers up, with the ATP sparks' soft pops; no motor, vroom or buzz (candidate A; B is a gas burner's steadier roar) (Sound C).

paramecium.said: (October 2, 2026, review) change the little shuffle sound at the beginning, maybe make it sound a little bit more like it's swimming, but not make it sound really windy
paramecium.note: Replace the opening shuffle with soft swimming strokes, not wind.
paramecium.plan: Now: A hand moving gently through water: soft strokes through its loop, no shuffle or wind (Sound C).

orbital.said: So for the electron orbital, I feel like we could make it sound a little bit more, like almost like electrical. I don't know how to describe that. I don't want it to be, like, totally unrealistic, but as the photon is, or I guess the, yeah, photon is absorbed and then sent out. It could sound a little bit more intricate. I don't know what the right word is. Right now it just sounds like a little chirp or something like that.
orbital.note: It's just a little chirp; it should sound a bit more electrical and intricate as the photon is absorbed and sent out.
orbital.plan: A short electric crackle and a rising swish as the photon is absorbed, and a brighter crackle and falling swish as it is given out.

atom.said: (October 2, 2026, review) The atom has, like, this vroom or motor kind of sound ... the sound that's on the periodic table that plays when I click the atom ... is almost perfect.
atom.note: No motor sound. Use the periodic table's atom-appear sound (a subtle electric one).
atom.plan: Now: The periodic table's atom sound: a soft electric blip as the electrons speed up and a ping as they blur into rings; no motor (Sound C).

molecule.said: (October 2, 2026, review) there's, like, a wind sound. We don't need the wind sound. And then for the kind of, like, building blocks sound, we should choose something different.
molecule.note: No wind; replace the building-block clicks with something better.
molecule.plan: Now: Soft little ticks of the atoms jostling as it heats, thinning out as it settles; no wind, no building blocks (Sound C).

protein.said: So for the protein, more or less what we're doing here for the animation is that, like, we're pulling the different parts of the ribbon apart, right? Right now it more or less sounds like wind or something like that, and then you can hear what sounds like building blocks. I'd like to make this more intricate. When it pulls apart, it should sound like something is kind of breaking apart or being separated, and then when it gets put together, it should sound like it's being put together. Right now it's a little too toy sounding.
protein.note: It sounds like wind and building blocks; it should sound like parts separating, then fitting back together.
protein.plan: A real tearing apart as it separates, with a whoosh, then a pressing-together and a soft thud as it reassembles (no building blocks).

crystal-lattice.said: (October 2, 2026, review) The sound is, like, metal chains or something. That's fine, I guess, but maybe we could make it a little bit better.
crystal-lattice.note: The metal-chain sound is OK; could be better (low priority).
crystal-lattice.plan: Now: One cleaner, softer metallic chime with a faint glassy ring, no rattle after (Sound C).

ruby.said: The ruby should have a different sound effect. Maybe for the ones that I mention, or just for all of the ones here that I don't tell you are, like, basically perfect, perhaps you could find, like, what a real gem of this type sounds like if somebody were to, like, hit on it or tap it or something like that. I don't know if they have a characteristic sound. … Maybe see if you can find something better for the ruby.
ruby.note: It needs a different sound: ideally what a real ruby sounds like when tapped.
ruby.plan: A lower real glassy tap and a warm low glow as it lights red.

diamond.said: Maybe for the ones that I mention, or just for all of the ones here that I don't tell you are, like, basically perfect, perhaps you could find, like, what a real gem of this type sounds like if somebody were to, like, hit on it or tap it or something like that. I don't know if they have a characteristic sound. I think the diamond, you can maybe find something for the diamond.
diamond.note: Find something better: ideally what a real diamond sounds like when tapped.
diamond.plan: A real bright glassy tap, and smaller tinks as the facets flash.

emerald.said: (October 2, 2026, review) there's almost like this wind sound, or whoosh sound, that's unnecessary
emerald.plan: Now: The crisp gem tap alone, without the whoosh (Sound C).

amethyst-geode.said: I think that the amethyst geode is basically perfect, so you don't have to worry about that one.

sapphire.said: (October 2, 2026, review) we don't need the wind or, like, sand shuffling sound
sapphire.note: Remove the wind and sand-shuffle sound.
sapphire.plan: Now: The crisp gem tap alone, without the wind and sandy shuffle (Sound C).

quartz-cluster.said: The quartz cluster I think is perfect. It's pretty much fine.

opal.said: Maybe for the ones that I mention, or just for all of the ones here that I don't tell you are, like, basically perfect, perhaps you could find, like, what a real gem of this type sounds like if somebody were to, like, hit on it or tap it or something like that. I don't know if they have a characteristic sound. … The opal definitely needs work. It sounds, like, robotic or something. You need to find something for that.
opal.note: It definitely needs work: it sounds robotic.
opal.plan: A softer, duller real tap and the stone rocking gently on the table (no synth shimmer).

pearl.said: I think the pearl is okay as it is.

crystal-ball.said: … also the sound for this is, like, too robotic. I don't really like it. We should change it.
crystal-ball.note: It sounds too robotic; change it.
crystal-ball.plan: A soft misty whoosh and a real crystal glass ringing as the sign rises (no theremin).

heart.said: (October 2, 2026, review) I can barely hear the heart beating ... If you could make it louder, but keep the sound, like the same
heart.plan: Now: The same real heartbeats at the same tempo, about 60 percent louder (Sound C).

brain.said: (October 2, 2026, review) It should sound kind of electrical, similarly to the neuron. ... a subtle current instead of this wind sound.
brain.note: Replace the wind with a subtle electrical current (related to the neuron's, not the same).
brain.plan: Now: A subtle electric crackle as the sparks race round (softer and lower than the neuron's), and a small snap as the side lights up; no wind (Sound C).

eye.said: The eyeball or the eye. So the sound here, of course, is when the eye blinks, and it sounds like sand or something. It doesn't actually sound like an eye blinking. The eye blink should be something a little bit closer to, like, a click than it is to wind. And this sounds more like wind.
eye.note: The blink sounds like sand or wind; it should be closer to a click.
eye.plan: A soft, small click as the lids close, and a fainter one as they open.

lungs.said: (October 2, 2026, review) Could you try to find different inhalation and exhalation sounds, just so I have something to compare it to?
lungs.note: Acceptable; try other inhale and exhale recordings to compare.
lungs.plan: Done (October 7, 2026): the owner picked B, a deep breath, in and out at the same strength; it is now the site sound.

tooth.said: The tooth is almost perfect, but that little whistle or noise at the beginning of the sound effect should just be removed. It's like a whistle. It's kind of awkward.
tooth.note: Almost perfect; remove the whistle-like noise at the start.
tooth.plan: A soft polishing swish instead of the squeak, then the same short gleam and sparkles.

kidney.said: So, like, the kidney is fine as it is.

oak.said: The oak tree is close, but the leaves falling don't really sound like leaves.
oak.note: Close, but the falling leaves don't sound like leaves.
